quick.topic: Delete what you do not need
quick.summary: Lower your security risk by automatically deleting records you no longer need.
quick.takeaway: Set a strict time limit for holding sensitive records and delete them automatically.

parts.title: Delete what you do not need

beats.line: We keep old user locations just in case. Is it safe to store everything?

board.text: Delete what you do not need

beats.line: Think of keeping old grocery receipts in your wallet.
It gets thick, it is hard to close, and someone might steal it.
Storing unneeded data costs money and increases your security risk.
Can I just say keeping things forever?
Delete anything that no longer serves a true business purpose.
Okay. So how long should we actually keep these logs?
You set a strict time limit based on what the law allows.
We only need locations for thirty days to check for errors.
Then thirty days is your limit.
After that window closes, the system must delete the records automatically.
What if a team complains they might need them later?
You ask them to prove it.
Without a current valid reason, holding sensitive data is a liability.
I will set the logs to drop after thirty days.
A lighter wallet is a safer wallet.

quiz.question: Why is keeping old sensitive data a bad idea?
options: It is a security risk and costs money to store.
It makes reports look too successful.
It legally belongs to your competitors after a year.
It requires you to hire more chefs.
quiz.explanation: Storing data indefinitely increases your risk of a breach while driving up storage costs.

quiz.question: A team should manually review and delete old logs every single day.
quiz.explanation: Deletion should happen automatically based on a strict time limit, rather than relying on manual reviews.
